utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to stop you there because Mr. Coric has 10 minutes and Mr. Prlic has 10 minutes, or rather their counsel, and we're not going to be able to get through that if you continue with your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the Court's indulgence, just one more question with regard to accommodation in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, the last question then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever hear about a concept which was relatively frequently mentioned here and also in the documentation of international organisations, the notion of exchange of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the other word.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What does that concept mean, what does the term mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since the population was Croatian, came to Bugojno, the civilian population, and took over the houses of Bosniaks in Prozor, then it was assumed that there was room in Bugojno for Prozor Bosniaks since the others were in our houses in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, madam. I'm not going to introduce myself. We don't have time for that. I'll start straight away. And I'll follow on from what my colleague before me asked you, and I'm going to ask you this: Where were you put up in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was accommodated in a friend's house in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: And the friends were in that house, too, with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The friends had two houses and we lived in one of their houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, please, and I'd like to go back to your statement, I'm sure you'll remember, and somebody already asked you that, I think, of my colleagues, you gave in a statement to the OTP, the investigators of the OTP on the 1st of June, 2002. You remember that, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to read out something from that statement of yours now. In the statement it says linked to the women that you interviewed, that's what this is about, and in the statement it says the following: "At the beginning of our conversation, I would tell them that I would take their statement secretly, confidentially, and that their husbands and families would not learn about the statement they had given." Similarly, the statement says, reads: "None of the women that I spoke to told me that they had filed a complaint with the authorities." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Could we briefly move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Let's say did one of the roads lead through Gornji Vakuf to Jajce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I can't remember what the roads were like. I know that they just said that they had come to help Jajce because Jajce was under threat.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Where is the road that leads to Jajce, madam? Does it pass through Gornji Vakuf? You're from that area. You must know which area the road passes through.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure where they were supposed to go. They all came claiming that they had to go to Jajce, but believe me, I don't know which road they used.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about their intentions. I'm asking you about geography. Does the road for Jajce pass through Vakuf? Is Vakuf between Prozor and Jajce? Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Vakuf isn't between Prozor and Jajce. Have you heard of a place called Karamustafic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a check-point of some kind in Karamustafic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of the troops in Prozor set off for Jajce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, I don't know whether they set off.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And my very last question: Perhaps you remember having seen a photograph that you recognised today. It was a photograph of Podgradje where you were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to call up the photograph now, but in that photograph can you see the location of the house you were accommodated in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see any houses in the vicinity of that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was outside the frame of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the woods that you hid in in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just have to have a look. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] It might be easier to see that photograph again. P 0794. Perhaps we could have it on the screen for everyone. P 0794. P 09 -- I see it's been incorrectly entered in the transcript. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the woods in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The part of the woods that we went to can't be seen here because the house was down below. It can't be seen in this photograph. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I? Still on the picture and the location of the house, was it to the left or to the right of the road one sees on the left hand of the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, madam. I want to touch upon a question that was posed by my colleague, Ms. Alaburic, and I want to go into it a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go into I guess a private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you for having come to testify at the request of the Prosecution in The Hague, and we wish you a safe trip home. Don't move until we have lowered the blinds. As far as the admission of documents is concerned into evidence on the part of the Prosecution, does the Defence have any comments to make? Mr. Kovacic -- or Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to two documents that are tendered. The list of houses and vehicles, P 09376 and P 00640. I believe that the witness was unable to confirm when the list was compiled or who the author was, so I don't think it's a reliable document. I'd like to point out also that I'm not sure whether the Prosecution intended to tender these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just for the record, these two exhibits have already been admitted on previous -- a previous session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's what I thought. Tomorrow, the hearing will start at 9.00, and two witnesses will be appearing. Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, shall we be tendering documents into evidence tomorrow for the witness Kljuic? However you decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, the best would be to deal with it tomorrow morning at the beginning of the hearing. We'll do that tomorrow as soon as the hearing commences. Thank you, and I will see you all tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 11th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
